title: Nonprofit Grant Pipeline Tracker

xlsx.example_rows_marked: Yellow fill + EXAMPLE prefix on funder/program names; README says to delete them.

cover.note: 1280x720 landscape matches every other Batch 12 cover. It is a Gumroad listing image, not a KDP cover.

cross_artifact_consistency: Guide names 12 must-pass eligibility questions; Eligibility sheet has exactly 12, matching in substance.
Guide names 12 standard documents; DocLibrary sheet has exactly 12.
Guide names 7 stages with exit gates; Stages sheet has exactly 7 with the same gates.
Guide's field dictionary matches every Opportunities header A-V, including the six computed columns.
Guide says DUE IN within 14 days (Opportunities) and 30 days (Timeline); formulas use 14 and 30 respectively.
Guide says closed statuses are Awarded/Declined/Withdrawn; both column S and helper column V use exactly those three.
Guide says Docs gap reads OK when nothing is required; column Q returns OK for 0 required.
Guide says awarded-above-max is flagged; column U contains that exact check.
Guide's worked example (15,000 award, quarterly reports, 57 days) is consistent with the Timeline formulas.

metrics_rederivation.method: Independent Python re-implementation of every computed rule (not an Excel recalculation - no LibreOffice in this environment).

timeline_next_due.next_due_expected: Check first due and repeat days

metrics_rederivation.result: All example rows match the expected states, day counts, duplicate flags and helper values.

limitations_disclosed: Workbook math was not recalculated by a spreadsheet engine: no LibreOffice/Excel is available in this environment. Formula logic was re-implemented independently in Python and the example rows agree.
The workbook was built for Excel and imports into Google Sheets in ordinary use, but no version-by-version editor matrix was tested.
No real funder's guidelines were used to validate the eligibility questions - they are a general screen, and the funder's own guidelines always win.
